0.0.n: Refers to the next stop in this bus announcement.

0.1.n: Marks 次 as the topic: which stop comes next.

0.3.n: This is the first fragment of まんまる, part of the shop name; it is not a separate word here.

0.4.n: This completes まんまる; る has no independent meaning here.

0.5.n: メガネ means glasses and 屋 means shop; together they form part of the shop name.

0.6.n: さん adds a friendly, respectful touch to the shop reference; it does not mean a person here.

0.7.n: Placed after the shop name, 前 identifies the stop's location.

0.9.n: This is the first fragment of まんまる in the repeated shop name, not a separate word here.

0.10.n: This completes まんまる; る has no independent meaning here.

0.11.n: メガネ屋 forms part of the shop name, repeated to announce the stop clearly.

0.12.n: さん adds a friendly, respectful touch to the shop reference; it does not mean a person here.

0.13.n: 前 follows the shop name and completes the repeated stop name.

0.14.n: Politely finishes the announcement identifying the next stop.

1.0.n: A quick exclamation on noticing something; small っ signals an abrupt ending.

1.2.n: The subject particle が is left out, which is common in casual speech.

1.3.n: Plain past form of 来る, used when noticing that the bus has just arrived.

2.0.n: This is the first fragment of まんまる, part of the shop name; it is not a separate word here.

2.1.n: This completes まんまる; る has no independent meaning here.

2.2.n: メガネ means glasses and 屋 means shop; together they form part of the shop name.

2.3.n: さん adds a friendly, respectful touch to the shop reference; it does not mean a person here.

2.4.n: Together with the shop name, 前 names the stop by its location.

2.5.n: Politely identifies the stop; the subject is understood from the announcement.

3.0.n: An exclamation showing the speaker is ready to act.

3.2.n: 乗ろう is the form of 乗る used to suggest an action or express an intention.

4.0.n: This is the first fragment of まんまる, describing the glasses' shape; it is not a separate word here.

4.1.n: This completes まんまる; る has no independent meaning here.

4.2.n: Refers to eyeglasses, with まんまる directly describing their shape.

4.3.n: Makes the statement about the glasses polite.

4.4.n: Seeks the listener's agreement or confirmation, with questioning intonation here.

5.0.n: A casual affirmative response, less formal than はい.

5.2.n: This is the first fragment of まんまる, enthusiastically confirming the shape; it is not a separate word here.

5.3.n: This completes まんまる; る has no independent meaning here.

6.0.n: This is the first fragment of まんまる, describing the shape; it is not a separate word here.

6.1.n: This completes まんまる; る has no independent meaning here.

6.2.n: Adds politeness to the description; what is round is understood from context.

0.lit: Next: in front of Round Glasses Shop; it is in front of Round Glasses Shop.
0.tip: まんまる is one word meaning perfectly round, despite being split into two tappable pieces.

1.tip: 来た is past tense, but here it announces a just-completed arrival: the bus is here.

2.lit: It is in front of Round Glasses Shop.
2.tip: Shop name + 前 names the stop in front of that shop.

3.tip: 乗ろう changes 乗る into a suggestion or intention: let's board, or I'll board.

4.lit: They are perfectly round glasses, right?
4.tip: ね asks the listener to confirm or agree with the description.

5.tip: うん is a casual yes, used with friends and others you speak informally with.

6.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject when context makes it clear.
